newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht falls on dollar rebound, interbank eases.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht falls on dollar rebound, interbank eases.

text.p: The Thai baht weakened early on Thursday, pressured by the firming greenback and a slowdown in dollar selling in the local market, dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 32.07/32.17 per dollar in the local market compared with 31.90/32.10 late on Wednesday, they said.
"The baht moved in a narrow range this morning with strong support at 32.30 level. We noticed that dollar selling was not as active as in the past two days," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"The upward tone of the dollar against majors seemed to trigger some buying from importers and corporates," he said.
Other dealers said players, especially exporters, might hold on to dollars, awaiting the central bank's monthly economic indicators later today before entering the market again.
"They might want to wait and see what kind of impact of the indicators will have on the market," said a dealer from a European bank.

The Bank of Thailand will release the monthly economic data at 1500 local time (0800 GMT). The data includes balance of payments, foreign reserves, trade balance, current account balance and money supply.
The baht was quoted around 31.650/31.850 in the offshore market, dealers said.
The interbank rate eased further to 12-16 percent early on Thursday compared with 15-17 percent late on Wednesday due to rising liquidity.
Dealers said ample amount of inflows entered the market via the swap market as the short-term swap premium dropped sharply.
"The tom-next swap (transaction which must be settled the next day) dropped sharply to around 3.00-4.00 percent," said a dealer from Thai Farmers Bank.
However, the interbank rate varied widely in the market as the liquidity was concentrated only in foreign and some major local commercial banks which still declined to lend to finance firms.
